title: [KDA] Fuse scaled_dot_kkt + solve_tril + recompute_w_u for KDA
body:
## Motivation
 
  This PR is inspired by https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21411. 

  The previous KDA prefill pipeline required three sequential kernel dispatches:

  1. chunk_kda_scaled_dot_kkt_fwd — compute the intra-chunk attention matrices (Aqk, Akk)
  2. solve_tril — solve the lower-triangular system on Akk
  3. recompute_w_u_fwd — recompute w, u, kg using the solved Akk

  Each step allocated its own intermediate tensors and launched separate kernels. By fusing steps 1+2 and calling step 3
  directly from the combined function, we reduce:
  - Kernel launch overhead (fewer dispatches)
  - Intermediate memory (no separate fp32 A tensor that is allocated, written, read, then deleted)
  - Data movement (the diagonal blocks stay in registers across the solve phase)

title: [Perf][Attention] FA2: split mixed prefill/decode batches into two calls
body:
## Purpose

On FA2 GPUs (SM8x: A100/A800/A10/A40/L4/RTX 30xx/40xx), `FLASH_ATTN` runs every mixed prefill+decode batch as one `flash_attn_varlen_func` call. FA2 has no tile scheduler; its grid is `ceil(max_seqlen_q / 64) × batch × heads`, so with chunked prefill each decode request launches `max_seqlen_q / 64` CTAs, all but one empty. The decodes also miss FA2's `max_seqlen_q == 1` path (packed GQA + split-KV), which only activates when the whole call is decode.

`sparse_attn_indexer` selects its top-k purely by indexer score. That is a density

1. **mhc_post_hc_head_fused** — 2-way fusion: MHC post + HC head
2. **mhc_post_hc_head_norm_fused** — 3-way fusion: MHC post + HC head + RMSNorm

- **PP > 1 safe**: The 3-way fusion is only applied on the last PP rank

## Purpose
Tune the `_num_warps` heuristic in the portable Triton **Gemma-RMSNorm** used by the MiniMax-M3 XPU path (`gemma_rmsnorm` / `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm`).

On Intel BMG/Xe2 the old heuristic selected 16 warps for the M3 hidden sizes (`BLOCK_N` up to 4096), which over-subscribes a single normalized row and regresses these bandwidth-bound kernels. The new ramp uses 16 only for `BLOCK_N >= 8192`, else 8/4/2. **Kernel math is unchanged.**
